subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Dream of Flying Cars
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Dream of Flying Cars usable.

hook.text: People have been promised flying cars since the 1950s—and every decade, the promise gets recycled.

buildup.text: Early attempts bolted wings onto cars, creating machines that were bad at flying and bad at driving.

discovery.text: The real problem was never technology—it was noise, safety, infrastructure, and air traffic management.

twist.text: Electric motors changed the equation—they're quieter, simpler, and allow vertical takeoff with multiple rotors.

climax.text: Over 200 companies are now developing electric vertical takeoff aircraft—eVTOLs—for urban air mobility.

punchline.text: Flying cars aren't cars with wings—they're helicopters that got quiet.

quiz.question: What technology made urban air mobility vehicles more practical?
options: Electric motors enabling quiet vertical takeoff
